findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The current implementation is vulnerable to path traversal attacks because it only strips the directory path using os.path.basename, but does not prevent attacks using relative paths or special characters. To fix this, we need to validate the filename to ensure it only contains allowed characters and does not contain relative path traversals. This can be achieved by checking for invalid characters and returning an error if the filename is not valid.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks by using a whitelist approach or a library like pathlib
findings.fixed_code: filename = os.path.basename(filename); if not filename or '..' in filename or '/' in filename or '\' in filename: return 'Invalid filename'; with open(os.path.join('/var/data', filename)) as f: return f.read()

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The security group allows unrestricted access to port 22, which is a critical vulnerability. To fix this, we need to restrict the ingress rule to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. By updating the security group resource, we can limit the exposure to only trusted sources.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: The AWS DB instance is missing logging configuration, which can cause important event information to be lost. Enabling logging by setting 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' will allow the instance to export logs to CloudWatch. This will provide visibility into database events and help with auditing and troubleshooting.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the AWS DB instance by setting the 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' argument
findings.fixed_code:
resource "aws_db_instance" "app_db" {
  identifier          = "app-db"
  engine              = "mysql"
  instance_class      = "db.t3.micro"
  username            = "admin"
  password            = var.db_password
  publicly_accessible = false
  storage_encrypted   = true
  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["error", "general", "slowquery"]
}

findings.title: EC2 instance has public IP
findings.description: The EC2 instance has a public IP assigned, which poses a security risk as it can be accessed from the internet. To fix this, the public IP assignment should be removed and the instance should be placed in a private subnet. This can be achieved by assigning the instance to a security group and subnet, as shown in the fixed code snippet.
findings.fix_hint: Remove the public IP assignment from the EC2 instance resource

findings.title: S3 access logging disabled

findings.fix_hint: Enable S3 access logging by setting the logging configuration on the S3 bucket resource

This can be fixed by adding the 'deletion_protection' argument to the 'aws_db_instance' resource and setting it to 'true'
findings.fix_hint: Enable deletion protection for the AWS DB instance to prevent accidental deletion

attack_chains.title: EC2 Instance Compromise
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains access to the EC2 instance using the security group's unrestricted SSH access, then uses the public IP to establish a connection and exploit the path traversal vulnerability to gain access to sensitive data.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses finding cfc3aba8 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf to gain SSH access to the EC2 instance
Step 2: this gives them access to the instance, which they can then use to exploit finding 7c0613ed in file src/app.py to gain access to sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access in the security group by updating the file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf

attack_chains.title: S3 Data Exfiltration
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses the dangerous IAM action to access the S3 bucket, then uses the lack of access logging and versioning to exfiltrate sensitive data without being detected.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses finding 9e40c93f in file iam/policy.json to gain access to the S3 bucket
Step 2: this gives them access to the bucket, which they can then use to exfiltrate data without being detected due to findings fd7e1df0 and f029771f in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf
attack_chains.remediation: Remove the dangerous IAM action from the policy file iam/policy.json

attack_chains.title: EC2 Instance and Database Compromise
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains access to the EC2 instance using the security group's unrestricted SSH access, then uses the public IP to establish a connection and exploit the path traversal vulnerability to gain access to the database instance, which has no logging enabled.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses finding cfc3aba8 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf to gain SSH access to the EC2 instance
Step 2: this gives them access to the instance, which they can then use to exploit finding 7c0613ed in file src/app.py to gain access to the database instance
Step 3: the attacker can then use the lack of logging in the database instance (finding 24e9ce32 in file infra/main.tf) to cover their tracks
attack_chains.remediation: Enable logging for the database instance by updating the file infra/main.tf
